title: The pattern A一+量词，B一+量词
pattern: A一+量词，B一+量词 (e.g. 说一句，笑一句)
simpleExplanation: A一+量词，B一+量词 describes two actions alternating or happening together, one measure at a time.
technicalExplanation: In this fixed pattern, two verbs A and B each take 一+measure: 说一句，笑一句 (say a sentence, laugh a sentence — talking while laughing), 走一步，看一步 (take one step, look one step — move cautiously), 吃一口，喝一口 (eat a bite, drink a sip). It stresses the alternation or pairing of the two actions and is highly idiomatic.
usage: 他走一步，看一步，非常小心。 (He took one step and looked, very cautious.)
avoidWhen: Do not add extra words between the verb and 一+量词.

title: The fixed pattern A这A那
pattern: A这A那 (e.g. 看这看那, 说这说那)
simpleExplanation: A这A那 repeats the same verb with 这 and 那 to show doing something to many things in a scattered way.
technicalExplanation: In the four-character pattern A这A那, the verb A is repeated with the demonstratives 这 and 那: 看这看那 (look at this and that), 说这说那 (talk about this and that), 问这问那 (ask about this and that). It conveys scattered, unsystematic activity, sometimes with a slightly negative or restless tone. The pattern is idiomatic and cannot be reordered as A那A这.
usage: 他到处看这看那，就是没买东西。 (He looked at this and that everywhere but bought nothing.)
avoidWhen: Do not insert objects or other words between the repeated verb and the demonstratives.

title: Degree adverbs: 特 , 异常 , 较为
pattern: 特 + Adj / 异常 + Adj / 较为 + Adj
simpleExplanation: 特 (especially), 异常 (unusually), 较为 (relatively) modify adjectives to express degree.
technicalExplanation: 特 as an adverb means 'especially/specially' and is colloquial: 特好 (really good), 特快 (very fast). 异常 is stronger and more literary: 异常兴奋 (extraordinarily excited), 异常天气 (unusual weather). 较为 is the formal counterpart of 比较 (relatively): 较为复杂 (relatively complicated), 较为安全 (relatively safe). 较为 typically pairs with disyllabic adjectives in formal registers; 特 is mostly spoken.
usage: 这次考试的题目较为简单。 (The questions on this exam are relatively easy.)
avoidWhen: In formal writing prefer 较为/异常 over 特.

title: Frequency adverbs: 一再 , 再三
pattern: 一再 + VP / 再三 + VP
simpleExplanation: 一再 and 再三 both mean 'repeatedly', stressing that an action happened again and again.
technicalExplanation: 一再 and 再三 are synonyms meaning 'repeatedly, again and again', used before verbs: 一再强调 (emphasize repeatedly), 再三提醒 (remind again and again). 一再 is slightly more general; 再三 commonly appears with verbs of urging, thinking, and considering: 再三考虑 (consider repeatedly), 再三要求 (ask repeatedly). Both are common in formal and written Chinese.
usage: 老师一再强调考试的重要性。 (The teacher emphasized the importance of the exam repeatedly.)
avoidWhen: Do not use them with single quick actions (that would be 一再 + process verbs only).

title: Manner adverbs: 不禁 , 赶忙 , 特地 , 特意 , 偷偷
pattern: 不禁 + VP / 赶忙 + VP / 特地|特意 + VP / 偷偷 + VP
simpleExplanation: 不禁 (can't help but), 赶忙 (hurriedly), 特地/特意 (specially, on purpose), 偷偷 (secretly) describe the manner of an action.
technicalExplanation: 不禁 means 'can't help but / involuntarily', often followed by emotion verbs: 不禁笑了 (couldn't help laughing). 赶忙 = 赶紧, 'hurriedly/quickly': 他赶忙站了起来 (he stood up hastily). 特地 and 特意 are synonyms meaning 'specially, deliberately', stressing that something was done for a specific purpose: 特地赶来 (come specially). 偷偷 means 'secretly/stealthily': 偷偷溜走 (slip away secretly). All four are adverbs placed before the verb.
usage: 听到这个笑话，大家不禁笑了起来。 (Hearing this joke, everyone couldn't help laughing.)
avoidWhen: Do not use 不禁 with volitional, planned actions.

title: 把-construction (4): agent as object
pattern: 主语 + 把 + 宾语（施事）+ 动词 + 其他成分

title: The pattern 不X不…，一X…
pattern: 不X不…，一X… (e.g. 不打不成器，一打吓一跳)
simpleExplanation: 不X不…，一X… pairs a negative condition with its immediate result when X finally happens.
technicalExplanation: This fixed pattern contrasts a suppressed state with its trigger: 不说不知道，一说吓一跳 (not saying — nobody knows; once said — everyone is shocked). The first 不X… clause describes what does not happen without X; the second 一X… clause gives the result as soon as X occurs. It is a compressed conditional: 'if not X, ...; as soon as X, ...'. The X in both halves is the same verb.
usage: 不说不知道，一说吓一跳。 (If you don't say it nobody knows; once you say it everyone is shocked.)
avoidWhen: Do not change the 不X / 一X structure; both halves must share the same verb.

title: The conjunction 不料
pattern: 不料，+ unexpected clause
simpleExplanation: 不料 marks an unexpected turn of events: 'unexpectedly, to one's surprise'.
technicalExplanation: 不料 is a conjunction (and adverb) introducing a clause whose content surprises the speaker, contrasting with what was expected: 本以为他会同意，不料他拒绝了 (I thought he would agree; unexpectedly he refused). It often follows a statement of expectation. It is a written/formal counterpart of 没想到.
usage: 本以为天气会好转，不料又下起了雨。 (I thought the weather would improve; unexpectedly it rained again.)

title: The preposition 除 (exclusion)
pattern: 除 (了) + X + 以外/之外 + 都/还/也
simpleExplanation: 除 means 'except / apart from', used to exclude one item from a group.
technicalExplanation: 除 is the formal marker of exclusion, usually appearing as 除了…以外/之外/外…. The frame can express: (1) exclusion — 除了他以外，大家都来了 (everyone came except him); (2) inclusion/addition — 除了英语以外，他还会日语 (besides English, he also knows Japanese). Distinguish by the adverb in the main clause: 都 marks exclusion, 还/也 marks addition. 除 alone (without 了) is very literary.
usage: 除了他以外，大家都来了。 (Everyone came except him.)
avoidWhen: Do not drop the closing 以外/之外 in formal writing.

title: Conditional compound sentence: 除非…才…
pattern: 除非 + Condition，才 + Result
simpleExplanation: 除非…才… ('only if… then…') makes the result conditional on an exclusive requirement.
technicalExplanation: 除非…才… expresses 'only if / unless': 除非你亲口道歉，他才原谅你 (only if you apologize in person will he forgive you), 除非下雨，比赛才取消 (the match is cancelled only if it rains). 除非 introduces the sole sufficient condition; 才 marks the result that follows only under that condition. The condition is framed as the only way the result can hold.
usage: 除非你努力，才能成功。 (You can succeed only if you work hard.)
avoidWhen: Do not confuse with 如果…就… (a plain conditional). 除非 adds 'only, and nothing else will do'.

title: Conditional compound sentence: 除非…否则/不然…
pattern: 除非 + Condition，否则/不然 + Result
simpleExplanation: 除非…否则/不然… ('unless… otherwise…') gives the negative consequence of missing a condition.
technicalExplanation: This variant of 除非 introduces a condition and states what happens if it is not met: 除非你马上出发，否则就赶不上了 (unless you leave at once, you'll miss it), 除非他道歉，不然大家不会原谅他 (unless he apologizes, no one will forgive him). Here 否则/不然 (otherwise) opens the negative result clause. The overall meaning: the result is avoided only by fulfilling the condition.
usage: 除非你马上出发，否则就赶不上火车了。 (Unless you leave right away, you'll miss the train.)
avoidWhen: Do not pair 除非 with 就 in this variant; use 否则/不然.

title: The pattern 到…为止
pattern: 到 + Time/Event + 为止
simpleExplanation: 到…为止 sets a deadline or boundary: 'up to ... as of ...'.
technicalExplanation: The frame 到…为止 indicates the endpoint of a period or process: 到现在为止 (up to now), 到月底为止 (through the end of the month), 到目前为止 (so far). title: The fixed phrase 得了
pattern: 得了，+ clause / VP + 得了
simpleExplanation: 得了 expresses 'enough / stop it / that's settled' and has several colloquial uses.
technicalExplanation: 得了 has two main colloquial uses. (1) As an interjection to stop something or end a discussion: 得了，别吵了 (enough, stop arguing), 得了得了 (all right, all right). (2) After a verb to mean 'just do it and be done': 走得了 (just go), 关门得了 (might as well close the shop). It conveys impatience or practical resignation. Note the pronunciation de liǎo vs déle differs by use; here it is déle.
usage: 得了，别再说了。 (Enough; stop talking about it.)
avoidWhen: Do not confuse 得了 with 得了 (de le) meaning 'caught it/got it' in a different pattern.

title: The pattern 东一A，西一A
pattern: 东一A，西一A (e.g. 东一句，西一句)
simpleExplanation: 东一A，西一A shows the same action scattered here and there, with no order.
technicalExplanation: The pattern 东一A，西一A repeats a verb/noun with 东 (east) and 西 (west) to express scattered, disorderly distribution: 东一句，西一句 (a sentence here, a sentence there), 东一堆，西一堆 (piles here and there), 东一榔头西一棒 (hitting here and there — a common variant). It emphasizes randomness and lack of plan.

avoidWhen: Do not use the pattern to describe orderly sequence.

title: The verbal measure word 番
pattern: Verb + 一/几/这 + 番 + Object

title: The pattern 放着X不Y

title: Conditional compound sentence: 凡是…都…
pattern: 凡是 + NP + 都 + VP
simpleExplanation: 凡是…都… ('every... / all... without exception') states a universal condition.

It is common in rules, announcements, and general statements.

title: The fixed phrase 好（不）容易
pattern: 好不容易 + VP / 好容易 + VP
simpleExplanation: 好不容易 and 好容易 both mean 'only with great difficulty', despite the negative looking like the opposite.
technicalExplanation: This is a classic trap: 好容易 (easy, literally) and 好不容易 (not easy) both mean 'with great difficulty / barely'. 我好不容易才找到你 = 我好容易才找到你 (it took a great effort to find you). The meaning derives from usage, not composition. The pattern usually pairs with 才: 好不容易才… (it was only with effort that...).
usage: 我好不容易才找到这家店。 (It was only with great effort that I found this shop.)
avoidWhen: Never interpret 好容易 literally as 'easily' in this fixed phrase.

simpleExplanation: 好你个X is an exclamation of surprise or reproach: 'you (scoundrel/clever one) X!'

title: Concessive compound sentence: 就算…也…
pattern: 就算 + A，也 + B
simpleExplanation: 就算…也… ('even if… still…') concedes a hypothesis while asserting an unchanged result.
technicalExplanation: This is a concessive compound sentence (让步复句) expressing 'even if': 就算失败，也不要放弃 (even if you fail, don't give up), 就算再忙，他也会回电话 (even if he's very busy, he still returns calls). 就算 introduces a hypothetical concession; 也 asserts that the result holds regardless. It is more colloquial than 即使…也…, which it equals in meaning.
usage: 就算下雨，我们也照常出发。 (Even if it rains, we'll set out as planned.)
avoidWhen: Do not use 就 in the main clause; the pattern requires 也.

title: The pattern 看/瞧+把+宾语（施事）+X得
pattern: 看/瞧 + 把 + Object + X得 (+ complement)
simpleExplanation: 看/瞧+把+宾语+X得 expresses 'look how X has made ...' with strong emotion.
technicalExplanation: In this exclamatory pattern, 看/瞧 (look) opens a 把-sentence whose agent-object undergoes state X: 看把你累得 (look how tired it's made you), 瞧把他高兴得 (look how happy it made him), 看把他急得 (look how anxious it made him). The complement after 得 describes the resulting state, which may be elaborated: 看把你高兴得合不拢嘴 (look how happy he is — grinning ear to ear). The 宾语 is the patient, not the subject.
usage: 看把你累得，快休息吧。 (Look how tired it's made you; rest a while.)
avoidWhen: Do not reorder to 把+宾语+X得 without 看/瞧 in this emotional pattern.

title: The pattern 看你X的/瞧他X的

simpleExplanation: 看你X的/瞧他X的 exclaims about someone's state or action: 'look at you/him, so X!'

title: Sentence-final particles: 啦 , 嘛
pattern: VP + 啦 / VP + 嘛
simpleExplanation: 啦 is a lively fusion of 了+啊; 嘛 marks an obvious or expected statement.
technicalExplanation: 啦 combines 了 and 啊, adding liveliness or a sense of 'come on': 走啦！(let's go!), 太好啦！(wonderful!). 嘛 is a modal particle that (1) states the obvious: 他本来就懂嘛 (he obviously understood all along); (2) marks a reason the speaker thinks should be clear: 这件事嘛，慢慢再说 (as for this matter, we'll talk later). 嘛 softens statements; 啦 adds enthusiasm. Both are colloquial.
usage: 太好啦！ (That's great!)
avoidWhen: Do not use 啦 or 嘛 in formal writing.

title: The fixed phrase 那倒（也）是
pattern: 那倒（也）是 + (comment)
simpleExplanation: 那倒是 (or 那倒也是) is a colloquial way of conceding: 'that's true / indeed, you're right'.

title: Class prefixes: 超- , 多- , 反- , 无- , 亚- , 准-
pattern: 超X / 多X / 反X / 无X / 亚X / 准X
simpleExplanation: Prefixes attach to a root to form new words: 超- (super/extra), 多- (multi-), 反- (anti-/reverse), 无- (without), 亚- (sub-/near), 准- (quasi-/accurate).
technicalExplanation: These morphemes behave like class prefixes in modern Chinese: they combine productively with both nouns and adjectives. 超- expresses exceeding a norm (超市 supermarket, 超速 speeding); 多- indicates plurality or multiplicity (多元化 diversified); 反- conveys opposition or reversal (反对 oppose, 反面 the reverse); 无- negates existence (无意识 unconscious); 亚- marks a level below the standard (亚军 runner-up, 亚健康 sub-health); 准- signals an approximation of a standard (准妈妈 expectant mother, 准时 on time). As bound morphemes they cannot stand alone; the resulting word's part of speech is normally inherited from the root.
usage: 这家超市的蔬菜很新鲜。 (This supermarket's vegetables are very fresh.)

pattern: 恰好 + VP / 倒是 + VP / 干脆 + VP / 明明 + VP / 总算 + VP
simpleExplanation: 恰好 (coincidentally), 倒是 (on the contrary / indeed), 干脆 (simply, just), 明明 (obviously), 总算 (finally, at last) add speaker attitude to a sentence.

title_id: Kata keterangan modal: 恰好, 倒是, 干脆, 明明, 总算
simpleExplanation_en: 恰好 (coincidentally), 倒是 (on the contrary / indeed), 干脆 (simply, just), 明明 (obviously), 总算 (finally, at last) add speaker attitude to a sentence.
simpleExplanation_id: 恰好 (kebetulan), 倒是 (sebaliknya / memang), 干脆 (sederhana), 明明 (jelas), 总算 (akhirnya, pada akhirnya) menambahkan sikap pembicara pada sebuah kalimat.
technicalExplanation_en: 恰好 marks an exact coincidence: 恰好赶上 (happened to catch it). 倒是 has two uses: mild contrast 'on the contrary / but' (他倒是同意了 he actually agreed) and emphasis 'indeed' (这倒是个好主意 that IS a good idea). 干脆 means 'simply, might as well': 干脆走吧 (might as well just go). 明明 emphasizes an obvious fact, often followed by a contrast (明明知道却不说 obviously knows but doesn't say). 总算 expresses relief that something finally happened: 总算结束了 (it's finally over).

title: The pronoun 人家

technicalExplanation: 人家 is a third-person pronoun with two main uses. (1) Generic 'others/other people': 人家都走了 (the others have all left). title: The fixed phrase 算了
pattern: 算了，+ clause / 算了 + 吧

title: Class suffixes: X-化 , X-式 , X-型 , X-性
pattern: X化 / X式 / X型 / X性
simpleExplanation: Suffixes turn a root into a noun or adjective: -化 (become/-ize), -式 (style/manner), -型 (type/model), -性 (nature/quality).
technicalExplanation: -化 is verbal/nominal and denotes a process of becoming (现代化 modernize/modernization, 自动化 automation). -式 marks manner or style (西式 western-style, 中式 Chinese-style). -型 denotes a category or model (新型 new type, 大型 large-scale). -性 derives abstract qualities from nouns, verbs, or adjectives (可能性 possibility, 重要性 importance). These suffixes are highly productive in academic and technical Chinese and frequently correspond to English '-ize/-ization', '-style', '-type', and '-ity/-ness'.
usage: 这座城市正在实现现代化。 (This city is being modernized.)
avoidWhen: Do not stack -式 and -型 with the same root unless the meaning is genuinely different.

title: Concessive compound sentence: 虽…，但/可/却/也…
pattern: 虽 + A，但/可/却/也 + B
simpleExplanation: 虽…但/可/却/也… ('although…, yet…') concedes one point while contrasting another.
technicalExplanation: This is a concessive compound sentence (转折复句) in formal style. 虽 introduces the concession, and the main clause uses 但, 可, 却, or 也: 虽下着雨，但他还是来了 (although it was raining, he still came), 虽小却有用 (small but useful), 虽贵也可买 (expensive yet still worth buying). 虽 is the literary short form of 虽然 and must be followed by a contrast marker in the main clause.
usage: 虽下着雨，但大家热情不减。 (Although it was raining, everyone's enthusiasm did not dim.)
avoidWhen: Do not use 虽 without a contrast marker in the main clause.

title: The structural particle 所
pattern: 所 + Verb + 的 + Noun / 为…所 + Verb
simpleExplanation: 所 turns a verb into a nominal phrase ('that which is verbed'), mainly in formal Chinese.
technicalExplanation: 所 is a structural particle (结构助词) used before a verb to form a noun phrase with 的: 所说的话 (the words that were said), 所需的东西 (the things needed), 所看见的一切 (everything that was seen). In the passive frame 为…所… it is literary: 为大众所欢迎 (welcomed by the public). It is often combined with 有/无: 有所提高 (has improved somewhat), 无所事事 (having nothing to do). 所 is mostly restricted to formal and written language.
usage: 这些是他所说的话。 (These are the words he said.)
avoidWhen: Do not use 所 in casual spoken Chinese; use a plain relative clause with 的.

title: Degree complement: 透 + 了
pattern: Verb/Adj + 透 + 了
simpleExplanation: 透 after a verb or adjective means 'thoroughly, extremely', closing with 了.
technicalExplanation: 透 as a degree complement (程度补语) intensifies a verb or adjective, meaning 'thoroughly/completely', always followed by 了: 衣服湿透了 (the clothes are soaked through), 苹果熟透了 (the apples are fully ripe), 这个人坏透了 (this person is rotten to the core). It usually applies to states that reach an extreme. Unlike 极, 透 implies 'penetrating to the end', and 了 is required.
usage: 雨下得这么大，衣服都湿透了。 (It rained so hard that the clothes are soaked through.)
avoidWhen: Do not use 透 with momentary verbs that have no extendable state.

title: The negative adverb 未必
pattern: 未必 + VP / 未必 + Adj
simpleExplanation: 未必 means 'not necessarily / may not', softening a negative statement instead of a flat no.
technicalExplanation: 未必 is a negative adverb expressing uncertainty or a weaker denial: 'not necessarily, not always so'. Unlike 一定不 (definitely not), 未必 leaves open the possibility. Examples: 他未必知道 (he may not know), 有钱未必幸福 (being rich does not necessarily mean being happy). It commonly answers or refutes assumptions: A: 他会来吗？ B: 未必。 (Will he come? — Not necessarily.)
usage: 有钱的人未必幸福。 (Wealthy people are not necessarily happy.)
avoidWhen: Do not use 未必 to state a certain fact; use 不一定 or 不见得 in colloquial speech for the same idea.

title: The pattern X到Y头上来了
pattern: X + 到 + Y + 头上来了
simpleExplanation: X到Y头上来了 means 'X has come down on Y', used when something bad falls on or is blamed on someone.
technicalExplanation: This fixed pattern expresses that an action, blame, or disaster lands on a specific person (Y): 这事怎么会到我头上来了？(how did this matter fall on me?), 他把责任推到我头上来了 (he pushed the blame onto me). The subject X is usually an action, problem, or responsibility. The 来了 adds the sense of 'has now arrived at (my) door'.

avoidWhen: Do not use the pattern for positive events; it carries a negative or burdened tone.

title: Alternative compound sentence: 要么…要么…
pattern: 要么 + A，要么 + B
simpleExplanation: 要么…要么… (either… or…) presents two mutually exclusive choices.
technicalExplanation: The pattern 要么…要么… introduces two alternatives in a choice compound sentence (选择复句): 要么你去，要么我去 (either you go or I go), 要么干，要么不干，别拖 (either do it or don't — stop dragging). The alternatives are usually exclusive and the tone can be decisive or urgent. Unlike 或者 (also 'or', softer), 要么 stresses a forced or clear-cut choice.

avoidWhen: Do not use 要么 for listing options without pressure (use 或者).

title: The auxiliary 也好
pattern: X也好，Y也好 / 就…也好
simpleExplanation: 也好 lists alternatives meaning 'whether X or Y' or concedes 'that's fine too'.
technicalExplanation: 也好 has two uses. (1) Listing alternatives with a neutral result: 去也好，不去也好，都得说一声 (whether you go or not, you must tell us). title: Parallel compound sentence: 一时…一时…

simpleExplanation: 一时…一时… (now… now…) alternates between two states or actions.

title: The pattern 这/那也不X，那/这也不Y
pattern: 这/那也不X，那/这也不Y (e.g. 这也不吃，那也不吃)
simpleExplanation: 这/那也不X，那/这也不Y complains that someone rejects everything: 'neither this nor that'.
technicalExplanation: The pattern repeats a rejection across 这 and 那: 这也不吃，那也不吃 (won't eat this, won't eat that — picky eater), 这也不好，那也不好 (this is no good, that is no good — hard to please), 这也不行，那也不行 (won't do this, won't do that). avoidWhen: Do not use the pattern for positive acceptance.

title: The preposition 至于
pattern: 至于 + Topic
simpleExplanation: 至于 introduces a new topic after mentioning another, meaning 'as for / regarding'.
technicalExplanation: 至于 is used to shift attention to a new topic, usually after something has already been said: 价格问题以后再说，至于质量，大家放心 (we'll discuss the price later; as for quality, rest assured). It signals 'as for, concerning', often with a slight reservation or contrast. Note 至于 also appears in the pattern 不至于 'it won't come to...': 不至于那么严重 (it won't be that serious).

avoidWhen: Do not confuse 至于 (as for) with 关于 (about, regarding a subject).

title: The fixed pattern 左A右B
pattern: 左A右B (e.g. 左看右看, 左想右想)
simpleExplanation: 左A右B repeats the same verb on both sides to mean doing it again and again from all angles.
technicalExplanation: The pattern 左A右B repeats a verb A/B (often the same verb) to express repeated or thorough action: 左看右看 (look again and again), 左想右想 (think it over and over), 左思右想 (ponder deeply). Sometimes A and B are different but related verbs: 左躲右闪 (dodge this way and that). It emphasizes thoroughness, hesitation, or trying many angles.
usage: 他左想右想，还是拿不定主意。 (He thought it over and over but still couldn't make up his mind.)
avoidWhen: Do not use the pattern with a single completed action; it implies repetition.
